- Current evaluation: you want a direct comparison vs your hyperscaler endpoints on the same model family (open LLaMA-variant) across production-like payloads.

Our proposed next steps:  
1) You run two short A/B benchmark runs (Redwood vs Hyperscaler) using the two payload sets we discussed (chat short prompts; long-context extraction).
2) Share p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and tail latency distribution + a sample of raw request logs (anonymized).
3) If results look good, we'll schedule a live co-run with our SREs to iterate on batching and KV cache settings.

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the artifacts — that's exactly what we needed. Quick notes after an initial pass through your CSVs:  

- Good signal: p95 improvement on Redwood (95ms) vs Hyperscaler-A (130ms) on medium prompts. The p99 gap (180ms vs 320ms) is particularly interesting for user-facing SLOs.
- Tokens/sec: Redwood's 280 vs Hyperscaler-A 200 is a significant unit-cost and throughput win for bursty workloads.

Recommended next tests (to isolate causes):
1) Controlled concurrency sweep: run 1,2,4,8 concurrent connections for each platform and capture p95/p99 and tokens/sec. This isolates scheduler/batching differences.
2) Long-tail stress test: 30-minute sustained run to observe GC/thermal throttling effects on the hyperscaler side.
3) Kernel/quantization parity: we can provide a matching quant profile — can you confirm the exact model artifacts you used?

We can schedule a live co-run Wed/Thu next week. I'll loop in our SRE (Vivek) and Solutions (Lauren) to help tune batching, KV cache TTLs, and to run a co-located test.

If you can confirm availability and the person on your side who will be executing the concurrency sweep, we'll send a precise test matrix and a short script you can run.

Thanks,
Marissa

Adding a quick note on economics and what to watch for during the sweeps:  

- Because Redwood's batching and prefix/KV cache reduces per-token work, you should see relatively flat tokens/sec at low concurrency and better tail behavior as concurrency increases. Hyperscaler-managed endpoints often prioritize median latency which can push up the tail when saturation occurs.
- Please capture per-token CPU/GPU utilization if possible and the cost per 10k tokens estimate for each run (we've included a sample cost calc in the shared doc).

If tests confirm the p95/p99 advantage, we can put together a Dedicated sizing proposal and an estimated cost delta vs your current hyperscaler spend for the same capacity.

Thanks,
Nikhil
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
